title: async kernel prober and coalesced prefill scheduler to cut host-GPU handshake
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Host-side overhead during prefill and decode (CPU-GPU handshake, memcpy spikes, and threadpool contention) contributes significant p99 latency for customer workloads that have mixed short and long prompts. Our existing kernel selection is static (based on model family) and kernel launches are serialized with blocking memcpy and synchronous fallback checks. This ticket implements an async kernel prober, a sequence-length histogram driven kernel selector, and a coalesced prefill scheduler to reduce CPU stalls, reduce memcpy fanout, and improve tail latency. Goals: 1) Introduce non-blocking kernel capability probing so prefill can speculatively pick an efficient kernel variant without blocking the decode pipeline. 2) Implement an in-memory sequence-length histogram sampler and fast path in the scheduler to choose the per-request kernel variant (FP16/quantized fused attention or fallback). 3) Coalesce small prefill requests on the host into burst DMA batches with scatter-gather transfer to reduce per-request memcpy overhead and avoid threadpool hot contention. 4) Add token-aware worker pools with bounded latency backpressure to avoid runaway thread growth under bursty multi-tenant load. Expected impact: reduce prefill CPU time by ~20-30% for mixed workloads, reduce p99 prefill+decode latency by ~10-18%, and cut memcpy peaks by >40% in microbenchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Async kernel prober implemented and exposed via runtime config (runtime.async_kernel_prober = true)
Sequence-length histogram driver selects kernel variant for >=90% of prefill streams in 1ms decision window in benchmarks
Coalesced prefill DMA reduces memcpy syscall count per second by >=35% vs baseline on our 8-GPU perf cluster
Token-aware worker pool prevents thread count growth above configured bound under synthetic spike test and maintains p50/p95 within SLO
Benchmarks: end-to-end p99 prefill+decode improves by >=10% on mixed prompt workloads (see grafana/perf/runtime-87456)
Unit and integration tests added; CI performance gate with representative workloads green
Design review completed and documented in Confluence: /confluence/rw/runtime/ENG-87456-async-prober
updates: 2026-02-12 - Ticket created by Maya Chen. Initial triage and scoping. Marked P0 due to customer p99 incidents this quarter.

2026-02-18 - Spike complete: microbenchmark shows speculative kernel probing can reduce decision latency from 2.4ms -> 0.6ms when preloaded with probe hints. Prototype attached: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/2987

2026-02-25 - Design doc posted (link in links). Chose approach: async prober + cached kernel table evicting on version changes. Trade-offs discussed: memory overhead of kernel table vs speed of decision; agreed to cap table size per-model to 128 entries.
2026-03-02 - Implemented coalesced DMA buffer pool and scatter-gather path. Early perf: memcpy syscall count down 42% on synthetic small-prefill workload. PR 3012 opened for review.

2026-03-07 - Threadpool change: added token-aware bounded workers and fairness queue. Integration tests flaked on Windows build due to thread affinity API mismatch; workaround added. Noted stronger effects on NUMA machines; will add NUMA allocator awareness next.
2026-03-10 - QA benchmark run against runtime-1.20 image: mixed prompt suite (50% short 16 tokens, 50% long 1024 tokens) shows p99 improvement 12%. Preparing rollout plan for canary in eu-west-1.

2026-03-13 - Security review requested (KMS unrelated) but data path change reviewed: no new customer plaintext exposure. Set security_review_required = false. Scheduling canary tomorrow with feature gate off by default.
